subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should user-explicit `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys bypass the sensitive-name sanitizer for host-run skill env while continuing to block dangerous host and loader-control env names?
rationale: The current bug is source-proven, but the repair changes which credential-shaped config values can reach `exec` child processes and therefore needs maintainer intent on the credential-to-exec boundary.

options.title: Allow explicit configured keys with hard dangerous-name blocks
options.body: Treat keys written under `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as operator-trusted for host skill runs, but continue rejecting dangerous host/runtime override names and add focused regression tests.

options.title: Require skill metadata declarations
options.body: Keep sensitive-name blocking unless each skill declares the exact env key in metadata, which is stricter but leaves bundled and third-party skills needing metadata updates.

options.title: Keep current blocking and document workaround
options.body: Document top-level/system env or wrapper scripts as the supported path, preserving the current security posture but leaving per-skill scoped secret injection ineffective for this use case.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit configured keys with hard dangerous-name blocks
recommendation.body: Treat keys written under `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as operator-trusted for host skill runs, but continue rejecting dangerous host/runtime override names and add focused regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show the strongest overlap with skill env regression repair and host exec env security policy.
